sampling_model.design: Deterministic absorbing staggered adoption with the untreated cells missing by a nested staircase after each unit's adoption date.
sampling_model.units: The inferential model is a complete triangular array in the note's exact-rank event-transfer class, with common regularity constants, fixed vanishing finite-slice envelopes, and independent centered sub-Gaussian errors on \(\mathcal Q_n^+\).  Variances are time-invariant within unit but may differ across units.  This is distinct from the published Choi--Yuan comparator, whose objects pair a law array with one selected scalar functional and use an approximately low-rank mean plus i.i.d. homoskedastic noise.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal effect is added after \(G_i\); the target averages eligible treated units with unit-share rather than equal-cohort weights.
sampling_model.overlap: Every eligible cohort-horizon block has donor-row and pre-period Gram eigenvalues bounded uniformly away from zero after size normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The feasible implementation uses blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals, unit-level residual variances, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers.  Oracle variance concentration is proved, while imputation contamination and the normalized rowwise loading discrepancy remain explicit through \(d_i\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\).  The generic band theorem conditions on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) and \(\mathcal B_n(h)\); neither event is made high probability by definition.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published model permits \(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+M^R\), assumes i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, and gives staggered scalar-functional normality under six hypotheses attached to one selected group, time, and partition.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact event-score corollary uses Proposition A.4 blockwise, while Proposition 1 proves that the published selected-functional class and the note's event-transfer classes are incomparable and identifies a nonempty common rank-one subclass.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Event-time aggregation crosses calendar times and factors, and the right-to-carry application motivates an adoption-aligned curve.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact staircase score and covariance plus a diagnostic conditional band protocol for the right-to-carry curve.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Multiplier bootstrap gives simultaneous staggered group-time inference under conditional parallel trends.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The retained headline is a finite-error generic remainder-event transfer under low-rank MNAR completion, conditional on score stability.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Data-driven intervals cover individual missing entries and attain an instance-wise scalar efficiency benchmark.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present note uses entrywise linearization only as input and makes no growing-curve efficiency claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Heteroskedastic pointwise intervals cover individual effects and scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under staggered adoption.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The score-stability theorem isolates the additional growing rowwise loading control not supplied by fixed scalar inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The corrected 2022 four-author Theorem 2.1 gives a singular-covariance-safe rectangle approximation of order \(\{B_m^2\log^5(pm)/m\}^{1/4}\) under sub-exponential and fourth-moment conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The headline verifies unit coordinate variances, fourth moment at most \(CmL_n(K)^2\), and envelope \(C\sqrt mL_n(K)\), yielding the log-power-five event-curve error and balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian anti-concentration permits honest confidence-band transfer without a fixed extreme-value limit.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The generic remainder event contributes \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}+Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\) in the explicit finite coverage bound.

tldr: The note's exact-rank, row-heteroskedastic model is now explicitly an event-transfer class, not the published Choi--Yuan class.  The eligible blocks aggregate exactly into one event-by-cell score, and a generic remainder event \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) yields a finite whole-curve error contribution \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}+Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\).  Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike's 2022 singular-covariance-safe theorem sharpens the Gaussian component to log power five and gives the balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).  Feasible growing-curve coverage remains conditional on the displayed remainder-event and score-stability probabilities.  The published approximate-rank, i.i.d. homoskedastic selected-functional class and the event-transfer class are incomparable; their explicit balanced rank-one common subclass is nonempty, but the attained nonlinear-remainder frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR inference treats one block, entry, or selected scalar functional.  Choi--Yuan's staggered Theorem 3.2 attaches six conditions to one chosen group, time, and subgroup partition; it does not provide a growing event-path remainder probability or the rowwise feasible-score rate needed here.  Generic high-dimensional approximation does not supply those panel-specific controls.
project_justification.niche: The useful bridge is a primitive-cell event score with exact staircase covariance and a generic finite-error transfer that exposes the nonlinear remainder event and score discrepancy.  Class comparison must be made after pairing the published law array with its one selected functional.
project_justification.fill: The note fixes eligible-unit weights, proves exact block aggregation and shared-cell covariance, concentrates oracle unit variances, and bounds covariance, scale, and correlation errors deterministically by the feasible-score discrepancy.  The 2022 CCKK theorem gives Gaussian error \(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4}\); anti-concentration adds \(Cu\sqrt{\log(2p)}\) on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\).  The Choi--Yuan bound enters only through \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) and its unsimplified source-submodel union bound.  An explicit proposition proves class incomparability and nonemptiness of a balanced rank-one common subclass.

related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, allow \(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+M^R\) with a globally incoherent low-rank signal and i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise.  Their published staggered Theorem 3.2 has six hypotheses for one selected \(\mathcal G,t_0,\{\mathcal G_\ell\}\), while Proposition A.4 supplies the one-block expansion used here.  Aggregation over growing eligible blocks yields only the displayed finite union bound.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022), Theorem 2.1, doi:10.1214/22-AOS2193, supplies the singular-covariance-safe fourth-root approximation with log power five.  The separate 2023 nearly-optimal theorem is not used because its covariance nondegeneracy condition is unavailable for staircase scores.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Lemma 3.1, supplies singular-safe Gaussian covariance comparison, and \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands} supplies anti-concentration.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, cover fixed scalar functionals under additional conditions, not the frozen growing rowwise score discrepancy.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate the right-to-carry event curve; Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, obtain simultaneous staggered paths under parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion.  Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, and Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, provide entrywise or scalar inference rather than this conditional growing-path transfer.
interpretation: For a right-to-carry event curve, the common critical value is justified only after the analyst controls the exact nonlinear remainder event and the realized score discrepancy.  Shared donor and pre-treatment cells remain in the full covariance.  Under balanced loadings, the Gaussian part allows \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\), but this does not certify either missing panel-specific probability.  A converse on the explicit common subclass would apply to the published model, whereas the event-transfer upper theorem does not cover published approximation bias from \(M^R\).
technical_internal_limitation: The primitive Choi--Yuan expression controls a one-block upper perturbation bound, not an attained nonlinear remainder and not a simultaneous heterogeneous-block event.  Its direct union bound may fail to vanish.  Variance replication controls the oracle residual squares but not the leave-one-cell-out imputation errors or the normalized rowwise loading discrepancy.  Therefore neither \(\|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) nor \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}(\log^{-2}(2K))\) is asserted over the event-transfer class.  The common rank-one array verifies both class condition families, but the estimator's exact signed second-order KKT expansion is absent from the frozen primitives; the early-kill comparison and attainable frontier remain open.  Approximate-rank upper validity would additionally need an explicit \(M^R\) bias remainder.
honest_scope: The causal target is the eligible-cohort unit-share event curve under deterministic staggered adoption.  Settled results are the exact eventwise influence identity, full staircase covariance, oracle variance concentration, deterministic feasible-score stability, and a generic finite-error Gaussian-multiplier transfer with the 2022 log-power-five approximation.  The Choi--Yuan specialization supplies only the deterministic inclusion \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) and an unsimplified i.i.d. homoskedastic source union bound.  Coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\) is conditional on explicit remainder and score probability limits.  The inferential event-transfer class is incomparable with the published approximate-rank selected-functional class.  Serial dependence, tuning selection, uniform feasible-score stability, simultaneous block probability, approximation-bias transfer, and the attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remain open.

definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ctr}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{subG}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{var}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rowvar}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{vrep}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{vrep}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rank}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{inc}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{sig}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{sig}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{spec}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{spec}})\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{block}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{block}})\wedge\mathsf A_A((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_B((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{nd}}((P_n))\wedge\mathsf A_{\mathrm{lev}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{lev}})\}\). Every member property holds at each finite \(n\) with the common event-transfer constants and fixed envelopes in the symbol table.  This exact-rank, blockwise-uniform, row-heteroskedastic class is not the published Choi--Yuan approximate-rank class; the superscript records the provenance of the block coefficients.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\)
definitions.construction: For each finite \(n\), define \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}=\{P_n: \exists (P_j)_{j\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\text{ whose }n\text{-th coordinate is }P_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) (band event-transfer class)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}:\mathsf A_{\mathrm{rem}}((P_n);\varepsilon^{\mathrm{rem}})\}\). Equivalently, each finite slice obeys \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{rem}}\) for the fixed vanishing envelope.  This condition controls only the deterministic primitive expression; asymptotic band validity still requires the separately displayed remainder-event and feasible-score failure probabilities to vanish.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\)
definitions.construction: For each finite \(n\), define \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}=\{P_n: \exists (P_j)_{j\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\text{ whose }n\text{-th coordinate is }P_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{event}}\)
definitions.construction: For every \(k\in\mathcal K_n\), apply the exact Choi--Yuan debiasing map to each eligible block \((g,k)\), then compute \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k})\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak C_n\)
definitions.construction: Map every eligible block to its exact Proposition A.4 donor-row and treated-preperiod coefficients, add the observed treated-cell coefficient, aggregate by \(n_g/N_k\), and return the array \(c=(c_{kq})\) defined in the symbol table.

definitions.name: \(\widehat\Omega_n\)
definitions.construction: On the variance-training set \(\mathcal V_n\), compute each untreated residual \(\widehat e_{it}\) from the rank-\(r\) Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing fit with cell \((i,t)\) deleted, and set \(\widehat\sigma_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}\widehat e_{it}^2\). Estimate the exact influence coefficients \(\widehat c_{kq}\), and set \(\widehat\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}\widehat c_{kq}\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u^2\) for all \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\); no variance-training cell outside \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\) enters this influence sum.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n\)
definitions.construction: For \(q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\), draw \(\xi_q\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\), compute \(W_n^\xi=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u\xi_q/\widehat s_k|\), take its conditional \(1-\alpha\) quantile \(c_{1-\alpha,n}\), and report \(\mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\).

definitions.name: \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\)
definitions.construction: After forming the finite slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), for \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) and \(0<\eta_n<1/2\), set \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)=\inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}\).

definitions.name: \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\)
definitions.construction: For every vanishing sequence \(\eta=(\eta_n)\) and each finite \(n\), set \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)=\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\), where \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) is the previously defined \(n\)-th slice of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).

definitions.name: \(\triangleleft\)
definitions.construction: For a candidate primitive envelope \(\beta_n(K)\) and the frontier output \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), define \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) if and only if \(\beta_n(K)/\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\to0\).

definitions.name: \(\Gamma_n(P_n)\)
definitions.construction: Set \(\Gamma_n(P_n)=\bigl[(1-\alpha)-P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}\bigr]_+\), using the uninflated conditional multiplier critical value.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\)
definitions.construction: Set \(N=8\), \(T=3\), \(r=1\), \(K=2\), \(G_i=2\) for \(i=1,\ldots,4\), and \(G_i=\infty\) for \(i=5,\ldots,8\). Set \(x_i=1\), \(z_t=1\), and \(\sigma_{it}^2=1\) for every cell. Thus \(I_2=\{1,2,3,4\}\), \(J_{2,0}=J_{2,1}=\{5,6,7,8\}\), \(S_2=\{1\}\), and \(N_0=N_1=4\). Apply the displayed coefficient formula for \(c_{kq}\) at \(k=0,1\).

definitions.name: second-order staircase alignment handle
definitions.construction: Expand the Choi--Yuan block KKT equations and debiasing map exactly to second order on balanced rank-one complete triangular arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), retain signed singular-space perturbations before applying norm inequalities, align their signs across nested adoption blocks, and optimize the resulting per-law quantiles over the explicitly defined finite slices to derive a primitive expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) equivalent to \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\).

definitions.name: RTC-law event-curve protocol
definitions.construction: On the 1977--2014 right-to-carry panel, retain the 44 states with at least eight pre-adoption observations, define \(G_i\) by the law's first effective year, apply \(\mathcal C_n\) to the eligible post-adoption subcurve \(k=0,\ldots,10\), retain \(k=-20,\ldots,-1\) as an observed pre-fit diagnostic outside the band theorem, and residualize the optional unit and calendar effects before block completion.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}_{\mathrm{sel}}\)
definitions.construction:
Let \(\phi_n=(\mathcal G_n,t_{0n},
\{\mathcal G_{\ell n}\}_{\ell=0}^{L_n})\) select one group-average
functional and a partition whose nonzero subgroups each share an adoption
date \(d_\ell\).  Define \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}_{\mathrm{sel}}\)
to be the class of complete pairs \(((P_n^{\mathrm{pub}},\phi_n))_{n\ge1}\)
with the following properties.  The untreated mean obeys
\(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+M^R\),
\(\operatorname{rank}(M^\star)=r<\min\{N,T\}\), the global singular
vectors \(u_i^{\mathrm{pub}},v_t^{\mathrm{pub}}\) of \(M^\star\) are
\(\mu^{\mathrm{pub}}\)-incoherent, its global condition number is
\(\kappa^{\mathrm{pub}}\), and
\(\max_{i,t}|m^R_{it}|\to0\).  The errors are i.i.d., centered,
homoskedastic sub-Gaussian with variance \((\sigma^{\mathrm{pub}})^2\).  Writing \(N_0\)
for the number of units untreated through \(t_0\), \(T_d\) for the
pre-adoption length at date \(d\), \(\psi^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\min,O_d}\) for the least
nonzero singular value of the corresponding observed core, and
\(\mathcal U_\ell,\mathcal T_\ell\) for the row and column sets of the
selected subgroup block, the following six conditions hold for the one
selected \(\phi_n\), for every \(d\in D_{\mathcal G}\cup\{0\}\) and
\(\ell=1,\ldots,L\):
\[
 \frac{\sigma^{\mathrm{pub}}(\kappa^{\mathrm{pub}})^{23/4}(\mu^{\mathrm{pub}})^{3/2}r^{3/2}\sqrt{N_0}
 \max\{N_0\sqrt{\log N_0},T_d\sqrt{\log T_d}\}}
 {\psi^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\min,O_d}\min\{N_0,T_d\}}\to0,
\]
\[
 \frac{(\kappa^{\mathrm{pub}})^{11/2}(\mu^{\mathrm{pub}})^3r^3\sqrt{N_0}
 \max\{\sqrt{N_0\log^3N_0},\sqrt{T_d\log^3T_d}\}}
 {\min\{N_0^{3/2},T_d^{3/2}\}}\to0,
\]
\[
 \frac{|\mathcal G_\ell|(\kappa^{\mathrm{pub}})^{17/4}(\mu^{\mathrm{pub}})^{5/2}r^{5/2}
 \max\{\sqrt{N_0\log N_0},\sqrt{T_{d_\ell}\log T_{d_\ell}}\}}
 {\sqrt{N_0}\min\{N_0,T_{d_\ell}\}}\to0,
\]
\[
 \max_{i\in\mathcal U_\ell,t\in\mathcal T_\ell}|m^R_{it}|
 =o\!\left(\frac{\sigma^{\mathrm{pub}}}
 {(\kappa^{\mathrm{pub}})^{5/2}\mu^{\mathrm{pub}}r\max\{\sqrt{N_0},\sqrt{T_{d_\ell}}\}}\right),
\]
\[
 c_1I_r\preceq\frac N{N_0}\sum_{i\le N_0}u_i^{\mathrm{pub}}(u_i^{\mathrm{pub}})^\top\preceq c_2I_r,
 \qquad
 c_1I_r\preceq\frac T{T_d}\sum_{t\le T_d}v_t^{\mathrm{pub}}(v_t^{\mathrm{pub}})^\top\preceq c_2I_r,
\]
and
\[
 \sqrt N\|\bar u^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\mathcal G}\|\ge c,
 \qquad \sqrt T\|v^{\mathrm{pub}}_{t_0}\|\ge c,
\]
for constants \(c,c_1,c_2>0\) belonging to the selected complete pair.
No uniform quantification over unselected scalar functionals is included.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak M^\cap\)
definitions.construction:
Define \(\mathfrak M^\cap\) as the class of complete selected pairs
\(((P_n,\phi_n))_{n\ge1}\) such that the law projection
\((P_n)_{n\ge1}\) belongs to the baseline event-transfer class
\(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), the pair belongs to
\(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}_{\mathrm{sel}}\), and
\(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^0=M^\star\), \(M^R=0\), \(r=1\), the global
rank-one loadings and factors are
balanced, and the errors are i.i.d. homoskedastic.  The selected
descriptor must be induced by an event block: for some selected
\((g,k)\), take \(\mathcal G=I_g\), \(t_0=g+k\), and partition
\(I_g\) into published subgroups.  Under this correspondence the
published donor core has \(N_0=|J_{gk}|\) and pre-adoption length
\(T_d=|S_g|\), whereas the event-transfer block has
\(N_{gk}=|I_g\cup J_{gk}|\) and \(T_g=|S_g|+1\).  Membership requires
both distinct families of inequalities: every uniform blockwise
condition in \(\texttt{def:cy-base-class}\) and all six selected-functional
conditions in \(\texttt{def:choi-yuan-published-selected-class}\).

statements.statement:
Fix \(n\).  For \(g\in E_k\), let \(b_{gk,q}\) denote the expression inside square brackets in the definition of \(c_{kq}\), let
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),
 \qquad
 \tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and define the exact block remainder \(r_{gk}\) by
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk}.
\]
Then the eligible-unit aggregation obeys the exact eventwise identity
\[
 D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
For \(C>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)=\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
 \{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), the deterministic implication
\[
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)
\]
holds.  In the i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel in which every eligible block satisfies the hypotheses of Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4, there are constants \(C,C_0<\infty\), common to the eligible blocks for all sufficiently large \(n\), such that
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 \le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
No assertion that the last sum vanishes, and no uniform \(O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) assertion over \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), is made.
statements.justification: This is the exact Choi--Yuan specialization of the generic remainder-event transfer: algebra gives the event score and \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\).
statements.gap: Proposition A.4 is one-block and i.i.d. homoskedastic; its honest growing-block consequence is the unsimplified finite union bound, not a class-uniform stochastic order.
statements.consumer: The generic headline substitutes the block event only when an analyst can make its displayed failure probability small.
statements.proof_tex:
For each eligible pair \((g,k)\), the definition of \(r_{gk}\) is an
exact equality.  The estimator and the causal target obey
\[
 \widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\widehat\tau_{gk},
 \qquad
 \tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\tau_{gk}.
\]
The second equality follows from \(N_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}n_g\) and the
definition of \(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\).  Subtraction and substitution
of the block decompositions therefore give
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}
   \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
All sums are finite, so they may be interchanged.  By
\(\texttt{def:staircase-influence-map}\),
\[
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}b_{gk,q}=c_{kq}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives
\(s_k>0\).  Since \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), division by \(s_k\)
yields
\[
 s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\sum_q a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q}
  +s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Comparison with the definition of \(\rho_{n,k}\) proves the coordinate
identity and the formula for \(\rho_{n,k}\); stacking over
\(k\in\mathcal K_n\) proves the vector identity.

On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), positivity of the cohort shares, the triangle
inequality, and the definition of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty
 &\le \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}|r_{gk}|\\
 &\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\\
 &=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus, for the generic event
\(\mathcal R_n(u)=\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le u\}\),
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
 \mathcal R_n\!\left(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\right),
 \qquad
 P_n\!\left\{\mathcal R_n\!\left(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\right)^c\right\}
 \le P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}.
\]
This is precisely the Choi--Yuan specialization needed by the generic
remainder-event transfer in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-multiplier-band}\).

It remains to prove the finite source-submodel probability statement.
Apply \(\texttt{lem:choi-yuan-one-block-remainder}\) separately to each
eligible block.  Its notation maps as
\((N_o,T_o,\vartheta_o)=(N_{gk},T_g,n_g)\).  For \(i\in I_g\), the cited
proposition decomposes the imputation error into the donor-column term,
the treated-row pre-period term, and an entry remainder
\(\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}\).  Since
\[
 Y_{i,g+k}-m^0_{i,g+k}-\tau_{i,g+k}=e_{i,g+k},
\]
subtracting that expansion and averaging over \(I_g\) gives the stated
block expansion with
\[
 r_{gk}=-\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}.
\]
Hence
\(\max_{i\in I_g}|\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}|\le
C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) implies
\(|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  In the stated i.i.d.
homoskedastic source submodel, the uniform block ratios and common
constants make \(C\) and \(C_0\) common to all eligible blocks for all
sufficiently large \(n\).  Therefore
\[
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}
 \le C_0\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
Boole's inequality over the finite collection of eligible pairs gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 &\le\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}\\
 &\le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is an unsimplified finite union bound.  Neither the source result nor
the event-transfer class makes its right-hand side converge to zero.

statements.statement: For all \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\), mutual independence and centeredness on \(\mathcal Q_n^+\) give the algebraic identity \[\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}\!\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{k'q}e_q\right)=\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2.\] Terms outside \(\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\) vanish by definition, and \(\Omega_{kk'}\ne0\) if and only if the displayed signed shared-cell sum is nonzero; individual products may cancel. Studentization is the identity \(\Sigma_n=D_n^{-1}\Omega_nD_n^{-1}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 U_k=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,
 \qquad k\in\mathcal K_n.
\]
All sums are finite.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) gives
\(E_{P_n}[U_k]=0\).  Thus, for \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\), bilinearity of
covariance gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}(U_k,U_{k'})
 =\sum_{q,q'\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
 c_{kq}c_{k'q'}E_{P_n}[e_qe_{q'}].
\]
If \(q\ne q'\), assumption \(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\) and
assumption \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) imply
\[
 E_{P_n}[e_qe_{q'}]
 =E_{P_n}[e_q]E_{P_n}[e_{q'}]=0.
\]
For \(q=q'=(u,v)\), the definition of \(\sigma_{uv}^2\) gives
\(E_{P_n}[e_q^2]=\sigma_{uv}^2=\sigma_q^2\).  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}(U_k,U_{k'})
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2
 =\Omega_{kk'},
\]
where the second equality is the definition of \(\Omega_n\).  By the
definition of \(\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\), every term indexed by
\(q\notin\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\) has
\(c_{kq}c_{k'q}=0\).  Hence
\[
 \Omega_{kk'}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}}
 c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2.
\]
This equality proves the asserted characterization: \(\Omega_{kk'}\ne0\)
if and only if the displayed signed sum is nonzero.  In particular, the
existence of shared cells alone is insufficient because products with
different signs may cancel.  Finally,
\(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives \(s_k>0\) for every
\(k\in\mathcal K_n\), so \(D_n\) is invertible.  The definition of
\(\Sigma_n\) then yields
\[
 \Sigma_n=D_n^{-1}\Omega_nD_n^{-1}.
\]

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\), the untreated mean has rank one, \(\mu_{2,0}=\mu_{2,1}=1\), \(A_{2,0}=A_{2,1}=4\), and \(B_2=1\). At each horizon, the four treated target cells have coefficient \(1/4\), the four donor target cells have coefficient \(-1/4\), and the four treated pre-period cells shared by both horizons have coefficient \(-1/4\). Therefore each marginal variance is \(12(1/4)^2=3/4\), each shared-cell covariance product is \((-1/4)(-1/4)=1/16\), the off-diagonal covariance is \(4/16=1/4\), and the correlation is \((1/4)/(3/4)=1/3\). This explicitly satisfies the noncancellation condition in \(\mathrm{lem:staircase\mbox{-}covariance}\).
statements.justification: The fully enumerated finite panel verifies the coefficient normalization and exhibits a nonzero signed shared-cell sum without appealing to an unnamed procedure.
statements.gap: No located low-rank staggered-adoption inference result displays this exact two-horizon coefficient calculation; the proposition is an algebraic witness, not a claim that a published method imposes block independence.
statements.consumer: The twelve-cell calculation is a deterministic unit test for implementations of the full RTC-law event covariance.
statements.proof_tex:
In \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\), the definition of the witness gives
\[
 M^0=\mathbf 1_8\mathbf 1_3^{\top}.
\]
Both vectors are nonzero, so \(\operatorname{rank}(M^0)=1\).  For either
\(k\in\{0,1\}\), the eligible block has rows
\(I_2\cup J_{2,k}=\{1,\ldots,8\}\), columns
\(S_2\cup\{2+k\}=\{1,2+k\}\), and every entry equal to one.  A compact
singular value decomposition is therefore
\[
 U_{2,k}=\frac{\mathbf 1_8}{\sqrt 8},
 \qquad
 V_{2,k}=\frac{\mathbf 1_2}{\sqrt 2},
 \qquad
 \psi_{2,k}=\sqrt{8\cdot2}=4.
\]
Because \(r=1\), the definition of block incoherence gives
\[
 \mu_{2,k}
 =\max\!\left\{
 8\left\|U_{2,k}\right\|_{2,\infty}^2,
 2\left\|V_{2,k}\right\|_{2,\infty}^2
 \right\}
 =\max\{8(1/8),2(1/2)\}=1.
\]
Every loading and factor equals one.  Since \(|J_{2,k}|=4\) and
\(S_2=\{1\}\), the definitions of the Gram matrices yield, identifying
one-by-one matrices with their scalar entries,
\[
 A_{2,k}=\sum_{j=5}^{8}x_j^2=4,
 \qquad
 B_2=\sum_{s\in S_2}z_s^2=z_1^2=1.
\]

For both horizons, \(E_k=\{2\}\) and \(N_k=n_2=4\); hence the outer
cohort weight \(n_2/N_k\) in the definition of \(c_{kq}\) equals one.
Moreover, \(\bar x_2=1\).  Substituting
\(A_{2,k}^{-1}=1/4\), \(B_2^{-1}=1\), \(z_{2+k}=1\), and \(z_1=1\)
into the displayed coefficient formula gives, with \(t_k=2+k\),
\[
 c_{k,(u,v)}=
 \begin{cases}
  1/4,&u\in I_2,\ v=t_k,\\
 -1/4,&u\in J_{2,k},\ v=t_k,\\
 -1/4,&u\in I_2,\ v=1,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The three nonzero cases are disjoint, and each contains four cells.  Since
the witness sets every cell variance equal to one, the definition of
\(\Omega_n\) gives
\[
 \Omega_{kk}
 =4(1/4)^2+4(-1/4)^2+4(-1/4)^2
 =\frac34.
\]
The treated and donor target cells occur at calendar date \(2+k\), so they
are distinct between horizons zero and one.  The only cells having nonzero
coefficients at both horizons are the four pre-treatment cells \((u,1)\)
with \(u\in I_2\).  Each such cell contributes
\[
 c_{0,(u,1)}c_{1,(u,1)}=(-1/4)(-1/4)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:staircase-covariance}\), whose independence and
centering hypotheses hold for the witness noise, yields
\[
 \Omega_{01}=4\left(\frac1{16}\right)=\frac14.
\]
Finally, the definitions of \(s_k\), \(D_n\), and \(\Sigma_n\) give
\[
 \Sigma_{01}
 =\frac{\Omega_{01}}{\sqrt{\Omega_{00}\Omega_{11}}}
 =\frac{1/4}{3/4}=\frac13.
\]
Thus the shared-cell signed sum does not cancel.

statements.statement:
Let \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\), which is positive under \(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\), and define the oracle residual variance
\[
 \widetilde\sigma_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2.
\]
There is a constant \(C_1<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\) and \(\bar\sigma\), such that, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}}P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|>
 C_1\left[\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}\right]\right\}\le2e^{-x}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 =O_{P_n}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}\right)
 =o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.  For
\[
 d_{it}=\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it},
 \qquad
 d_i^2=h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2,
\]
the feasible residual variance has the exact contamination bound
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2|
 \le2\left(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i+d_i^2.
\]
Finally, set
\[
 \widehat b_{kq}=\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u/s_k,
 \qquad
 r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left\{\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
 (\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right\}^{1/2},
\]
and \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), with \(\delta_h=2h+h^2<1\),
\[
 \max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}\le\delta_h,
 \qquad
 \max_k\left|\frac{\widehat s_k}{s_k}-1\right|
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
\]
These are deterministic consequences of the displayed score discrepancy.  No stochastic rate for \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem separates the variance component that replication identifies from the imputation and loading components that the frozen assumptions do not control.
statements.gap: Available feasible low-rank central limit theorems concern fixed functionals and do not establish the growing normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) score rate required by this plug-in covariance.
statements.consumer: The deterministic map \(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\mapsto(\widehat\Omega,\widehat s,\widehat\Sigma)\) is the feasible covariance input to the conditional multiplier comparison.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(h_{\min}=\min_{i\le N}h_i\).  By the definitions of
\(\mathcal V_n\) and \(h_i\),
\[
 \min_{i\le N}|\{t:(i,t)\in\mathcal V_n\}|=h_{\min}.
\]
The real-valued inequality in \(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) has
this quantity in its denominator; hence that assumption entails
\(h_{\min}>0\).  Thus every oracle average in the statement is well
defined.

Fix \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\), for every \(t\in H_i\),
\[
 E_{P_n}[e_{it}^2]=\sigma_{it}^2=\sigma_i^2.
\]
We first establish the claimed concentration uniformly over the finite
slices.  The definition of the sub-Gaussian norm and
\(\texttt{ass:heteroskedastic-subgaussian}\) imply that there is a
constant \(C_2<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such that
\[
 E_{P_n}\exp\!\left\{\frac{e_{it}^2}{C_2\sigma_i^2}\right\}\le2.
\]
For every integer \(m\ge1\), the elementary inequality
\(y^m\le m!e^y\), applied with
\(y=e_{it}^2/(C_2\sigma_i^2)\), gives
\[
 E_{P_n}|e_{it}|^{2m}
 \le 2m!(C_2\sigma_i^2)^m.
\]
Set \(U_{it}=e_{it}^2-\sigma_i^2\).  Then
\(E_{P_n}[U_{it}]=0\).  The preceding moment inequality,
\((x+y)^m\le2^{m-1}(x^m+y^m)\) for \(x,y\ge0\), and
\(\sigma_i\le\bar\sigma\) from \(\texttt{ass:variance-bounds}\) imply
that a constant \(C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), satisfies
\[
 E_{P_n}|U_{it}|^m\le m!(C_3\bar\sigma^2)^m,
 \qquad m\ge2.
\]
Let \(B=C_3\bar\sigma^2\).  Expanding the exponential, using
\(E_{P_n}[U_{it}]=0\), and bounding every remaining signed moment by its
absolute moment shows that, whenever \(|\lambda|B\le1/2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_n}e^{\lambda U_{it}}
 &\le 1+\sum_{m=2}^{\infty}(|\lambda|B)^m\\
 &\le 1+2\lambda^2B^2
 \le \exp(2\lambda^2B^2).
 \end{aligned}
\]

For a fixed unit \(i\), assumption \(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\)
makes \(\{U_{it}:t\in H_i\}\) mutually independent.  Multiplication of
the preceding moment-generating-function bounds therefore gives
\[
 E_{P_n}\exp\!\left\{\lambda\sum_{t\in H_i}U_{it}\right\}
 \le \exp(2h_i\lambda^2B^2),
 \qquad |\lambda|B\le1/2.
\]
Exponential Markov inequality, first with positive \(\lambda\) and then
with negative \(\lambda\), and the choice of \(|\lambda|\) proportional
to
\[
 \min\!\left\{\frac{\sqrt y}{B\sqrt{h_i}},\frac1B\right\}
\]
show that there is a constant \(C_4<\infty\), depending only on
\(C_e\) and \(\bar\sigma\), for which, for every \(y\ge0\),
\[
 P_n\!\left\{
 \left|h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}U_{it}\right|
 >C_4\left(\sqrt{\frac y{h_i}}+\frac y{h_i}\right)
 \right\}\le2e^{-y}.
\]
Because
\(h_i^{-1}\sum_{t\in H_i}U_{it}=\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2\),
we may take \(y=\log(2N)+x\), use \(h_i\ge h_{\min}\), and apply the
union bound over \(i\le N\).  This yields
\[
 P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 >C_4\left[
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)+x}{h_{\min}}
 \right]\right\}
 \le 2N e^{-\log(2N)-x}=e^{-x}\le2e^{-x}.
\]
The constants used above do not depend on \(P_n\), \(i\), or \(n\).
Taking the supremum over \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) proves the
first assertion with \(C_1=C_4\).

For completeness, taking \(x=\log(2/\delta)\) in the preceding display,
for arbitrary fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\), proves uniformly over the finite
slices that
\[
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 =O_{P_n}\!\left(
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}}
 +\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}
 \right).
\]
Indeed, \(\log(2N)\ge\log2\), so the fixed additive term
\(\log(2/\delta)\) can be absorbed into a \(\delta\)-dependent
multiplicative constant.  Put
\[
 v_n=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N)}{h_{\min}}}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:variance-replication}\) states
\[
 v_n\log^2(2K)\le\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
It also implies \(v_n\to0\), since \(\log(2K)\ge\log2\).  Therefore
\[
 (v_n+v_n^2)\log^2(2K)
 \le \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{vrep}}(1+v_n)longrightarrow0.
\]
Combining this deterministic relation with the uniform stochastic order
proves
\[
 \max_{i\le N}|\widetilde\sigma_i^2-\sigma_i^2|
 =o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})
\]
uniformly over the finite slices.

We next isolate imputation contamination.  For \(t\in H_i\), the cell is
untreated by definition of \(H_i\).  The observation equation consequently
reduces to \(Y_{it}=m^0_{it}+e_{it}\).  With
\(d_{it}=\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}-m^0_{it}\), the definition of the
leave-one-cell-out residual gives
\[
 \widehat e_{it}=Y_{it}-\widehat m_{it}^{0,(-it)}=e_{it}-d_{it}.
\]
Expanding the square exactly yields
\[
 \widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2
 =-\frac2{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}
 +\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz and the definition of \(d_i\),
\[
 \left|\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}d_{it}\right|
 \le
 \left(\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}d_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}
 =\left(\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i.
\]
The triangle inequality proves
\[
 |\widehat\sigma_i^2-\widetilde\sigma_i^2|
 \le2\left(\frac1{h_i}\sum_{t\in H_i}e_{it}^2\right)^{1/2}d_i+d_i^2.
\]
No frozen assumption supplies a stochastic bound for \(d_i\), so the
argument makes no stronger feasible-variance assertion.

It remains to prove the deterministic score-stability conclusions.  By
\(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\), if \(q=(u,v)\), then
\(\sigma_{uv}=\sigma_u\).  The definitions of \(a_{kq}\), \(s_k\), and
\(\Omega_{kk}\), together with \(s_k>0\) from
\(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\), imply
\[
 \|a_k\|_2^2
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}^2
 =s_k^{-2}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}^2\sigma_u^2
 =s_k^{-2}\Omega_{kk}=1.
\]
By the definitions of \(\widehat b_{kq}\), \(\widehat\Omega_n\), and
\(\Omega_n\),
\[
 \frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q},
 \qquad
 \frac{\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\sum_qa_{kq}a_{k'q}.
\]
Set \(u_k=\widehat b_k-a_k\).  Subtracting the two inner products gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}}
 =\langle u_k,a_{k'}\rangle
 +\langle a_k,u_{k'}\rangle
 +\langle u_k,u_{k'}\rangle.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), one has \(\|u_j\|_2\le h\) for every
\(j\in\mathcal K_n\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\|a_j\|_2=1\) therefore
give
\[
 \max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}
 \frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}
 \le h+h+h^2=\delta_h.
\]

Set \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  The diagonal case of the last bound gives
\[
 |t_k^2-1|
 =\left|\frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk}-\Omega_{kk}}{s_k^2}\right|
 \le\delta_h.
\]
If \(\delta_h<1\), then
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}>0\), so every feasible standard error is
positive and \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) is well defined.  Moreover,
\[
 |t_k-1|
 =\frac{|t_k^2-1|}{t_k+1}
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h}}.
\]
For any \(k,k'\), the bounds on \(t_k^2\) and \(t_{k'}^2\) imply
\[
 1-\delta_h\le t_kt_{k'}\le1+\delta_h.
\]
Also \(|\Sigma_{kk'}|\le1\) by Cauchy--Schwarz because \(\Sigma_n\) is
the Gram matrix of the unit vectors \(a_k\).  If
\[
 E_{kk'}=
 \frac{\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}}{s_ks_{k'}},
\]
then \(|E_{kk'}|\le\delta_h\) and
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_{kk'}
 =\frac{\Sigma_{kk'}+E_{kk'}}{t_kt_{k'}}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}-\Sigma_{kk'}|
 &\le \frac{|E_{kk'}|}{t_kt_{k'}}
 +|\Sigma_{kk'}|\frac{|1-t_kt_{k'}|}{t_kt_{k'}}\\
 &\le\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 +\frac{\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}
 =\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Taking the maximum over \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\) proves the final claim.
Every assertion after the definition of \(\mathcal B_n(h)\) is therefore
a deterministic implication of the score discrepancy, as required.

statements.statement:
Let \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\ge3\), \(p=2K\ge2\),
\(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\), and
\[
 S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\epsilon_q.
\]
After arbitrarily ordering the cells, define the sign-expanded vectors
\[
 X_q=\sqrt m\,(a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,
 a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q,-a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,
 -a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q)\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Then \(m^{-1/2}\sum_qX_q\) has maximum
\(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\).  For every coordinate \(j\le p\),
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2=1,
 \qquad
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4
 \le C mL_n(K)^2,
 \qquad
 \|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}\le C\sqrt mL_n(K).
\]
There is a constant \(C_1<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such
that, with
\[
 \mathfrak g_n=C_1\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4},
 \qquad M_n^Z=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|,
\]
one has
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|
 \le\mathfrak g_n.
\]
The \(p\)-dimensional Gaussian covariance in this comparison is the
sign expansion induced by \(\Sigma_n\), and may be singular.

For \(u\ge0\), define the exact remainder event
\[
 \mathcal R_n(u)=\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le u\}.
\]
For \(h\ge0\), let \(\mathcal B_n(h)\) and
\(\delta_h=2h+h^2\) be as in
\(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\), set
\(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\), and, when \(h>0\), set
\[
 \mathfrak c_n(h)=C_3\delta_h^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}.
\]
There are constants \(C_2,C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\),
such that whenever \(0\le\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_k\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}
 \le z\right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le \mathfrak g_n+P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}
 +C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), conditionally on \(Y\), \(W_n^\xi\) is
exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of
\(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\), and
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le\mathfrak c_n(h).
\]
If \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}
 \text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\\
 &\quad\le1\wedge\Big[\mathfrak g_n
 +P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}+2P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\hspace{35mm}+C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +2\mathfrak c_n(h)\Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, along any complete array in the baseline event-transfer
class, asymptotic coverage follows if deterministic \(u_n,h_n\downarrow0\)
satisfy
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\to0,
 \quad P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \quad u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0,
 \quad h_n\log^2(2p)\to0.
\]
For the Choi--Yuan specialization,
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\) permits
\(u_n=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) and replaces
\(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\) by the larger displayed probability
\(P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}\).  Thus, along an array in the band
event-transfer class, coverage tends to \(1-\alpha\) only if this block
failure probability and the score failure probability also vanish at the
displayed rates.  Finally, under balanced loadings
\(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), the Gaussian-approximation term vanishes under
the elbow condition
\[
 \log(Km)=o(m^{1/5}).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) permits
division by every \(s_k\).  By the definitions of \(s_k\) and \(a_{kq}\),
\[
 \sum_q a_{kq}^2
 =s_k^{-2}\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_q^2=1.
\]
Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\) make the vectors \(X_q\) independent
and centered.  Since \(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^2=1\), every sign-expanded
coordinate \(j\) associated with a horizon \(k\) satisfies
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2
 =\sum_q a_{kq}^2=1.
\]
Uniform sub-Gaussianity gives
\(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^4\le C\) and
\(\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_1}\le\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\).
Using \(|a_{kq}|\le L_n(K)\) and \(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4
 &=m\sum_qa_{kq}^4E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^4\\
 &\le CmL_n(K)^2\sum_qa_{kq}^2
 =CmL_n(K)^2,
 \end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
 \|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}
 \le C\sqrt m\,|a_{kq}|
 \le C\sqrt mL_n(K).
\]
Because \(1=\sum_qa_{kq}^2\le mL_n(K)^2\), the envelope
\(B_m=C\sqrt mL_n(K)\) can be chosen at least one.  Thus the variance,
fourth-moment, and sub-exponential hypotheses of
\(\texttt{lem:cckk2022-gaussian-approximation}\) hold with constants
depending only on \(C_e\).  That cited theorem applies because
\(m\ge3\) and \(p\ge2\), and yields
\[
 C\left\{\frac{B_m^2\log^5(pm)}m\right\}^{1/4}
 \le C_1\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4}
 =\mathfrak g_n.
\]
The normalized sum has coordinate list
\((S_{n,0},\ldots,S_{n,K-1},-S_{n,0},\ldots,-S_{n,K-1})\), so its
maximum is \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\).  Its first \(K\) coordinates have
covariance
\[
 \sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}=\Sigma_{n,kk'}
\]
by \(\texttt{lem:staircase-covariance}\); hence its full Gaussian
covariance is the sign expansion induced by \(\Sigma_n\), not the
\(K\)-by-\(K\) matrix itself.  The cited result requires only the unit
coordinate variances established above and therefore permits singular
covariance.

We transfer this comparison to the feasible statistic.  Write
\(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\),
\(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\) gives
\(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  If \(\delta_h\le1/2\), then
\(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}\), \(t_k^{-1}\le\sqrt2\), and
\[
 |t_k^{-1}-1|
 =\frac{|t_k-1|}{t_k}
 \le\frac{\delta_h}
 {(1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h})\sqrt{1-\delta_h}}
 \le\delta_h.
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\),
\[
 \max_k\left|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})-S_{n,k}\right|
 \le\delta_h\max_k|S_{n,k}|+\sqrt2u.
\]
Independence, the sub-Gaussian moment-generating-function bound, and
\(\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1\) imply
\[
 P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|>C_4\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}\}
 \le\delta_h
\]
for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\).  On the complementary event the last
perturbation is at most
\[
 v_n=C_5\{\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}+u\}.
\]
The Gaussian vector has unit marginal variances.  Hence
\(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-anti-concentration}\) gives
\[
 \sup_zP\{|M_n^Z-z|\le v_n\}
 \le Cv_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}.
\]
Sandwich the feasible event between linear events at thresholds
\(z-v_n\) and \(z+v_n\), then use the Gaussian approximation.  Adding
the two failure probabilities and the tail probability \(\delta_h\)
gives the asserted distribution bound after using, for
\(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \delta_h+
 \delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}
 \le C\left[\delta_h\log(2p)+
 \delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}\right].
\]
This elementary inequality follows by splitting
\(\log(2p/\delta_h)=\log(2p)+\log(1/\delta_h)\), applying
\(2\sqrt{ab}\le a+b\), and using
\(x\log(1/x)=O(x^{1/3})\) on \((0,1/2]\).  When \(h=0\), scale error
is zero and the same bound follows directly with
\(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\).

For the multiplier comparison, conditional on \(Y\), independence and
Gaussianity of \(\xi_q\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q,
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_{k'}}\xi_q
 \mathrel{\Big|}Y\right)=\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}.
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi\) is conditionally the maximum absolute coordinate of
\(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\),
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}\le4\delta_h.
\]
Apply \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-comparison-maxima}\) to the two
sign-expanded Gaussian vectors.  Its coordinate variances are bounded
and it permits singular covariance, so
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le\mathfrak c_n(h).
\]

The maximum of finitely many absolute Gaussian coordinates with positive
marginal variances has no atoms: for every \(z\), its atom is bounded by
the sum of the zero point-masses of the individual absolute Gaussian
coordinates.  Its distribution function is therefore continuous.  On
\(\mathcal B_n(h)\), Gaussian comparison brackets the conditional
\((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(W_n^\xi\) between the
\((1-\alpha-\mathfrak c_n(h))\)- and
\((1-\alpha+\mathfrak c_n(h))\)-quantiles of \(M_n^Z\).  Evaluating the
feasible distribution bound at those two deterministic quantiles and
paying \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\) once more proves the finite coverage
inequality.

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:cell-leverage}\) makes \(\mathfrak g_n\to0\).
If \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\), then
\(\delta_{h_n}\log(2p)\to0\) and
\(\delta_{h_n}\log^2(p/\delta_{h_n})\to0\), so
\(\mathfrak c_n(h_n)\to0\).  The generic asymptotic statement follows
by inserting the four displayed remainder and score conditions into the
finite bound.  For the Choi--Yuan specialization,
\(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) was proved in
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\), and
\(\texttt{ass:uniform-remainder-envelope}\) makes its deterministic
anti-concentration term vanish.  The two failure probabilities remain
additional premises.  Finally, if \(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), then
\(\mathfrak g_n\to0\) whenever
\(m^{-1}\log^5((p\vee3)m)\to0\), equivalently
\(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\), proving the elbow statement.

statements.gap: A growing-path theorem still needs high-probability control of the exact nonlinear remainder event and feasible score discrepancy; neither follows from the class label.

statements.statement: When \(K=1\), \(\mathcal K_n=\{0\}\), the eligible set contains one target block \(E_0=\{g_0\}\), and \(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\), \(c_{0q}\) and \(\Omega_{00}\) reduce to the Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 influence coefficients and their heteroskedastic scalar influence variance, while \(\widehat\Omega_{00}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,0}\) reduce to the Choi--Kwon--Liao-style unit-residual plug-in variance and the ordinary studentized scalar interval.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume the hypotheses in the proposition.  Because \(g_0\) is a realized
finite adoption cohort, \(I_{g_0}\neq\varnothing\), and hence
\(n_{g_0}=|I_{g_0}|\geq 1\).  Thus all cohort averages below are defined.
Since \(E_0=\{g_0\}\), the definition of \(N_k\) gives
\[
N_0=\sum_{g\in E_0}n_g=n_{g_0},
\qquad
\frac{n_{g_0}}{N_0}=1.
\]
Substituting \(k=0\), \(E_0=\{g_0\}\), and this last equality into the
coefficient array defined by \(\texttt{def:staircase-influence-map}\) yields,
for every \(q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_{0,(u,v)}
={}&\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_{g_0},\ v=g_0\}}{n_{g_0}}
-\mathbf 1\{u\in J_{g_0,0},\ v=g_0\}
  \bar x_{g_0}^{\top}A_{g_0,0}^{-1}x_u \\
&-\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_{g_0},\ v\in S_{g_0}\}}{n_{g_0}}
  z_{g_0}^{\top}B_{g_0}^{-1}z_v .
\end{aligned}
\]
The three terms are respectively the observed treated-cell, target-column
donor-row, and treated-row preperiod coefficients of the single eligible
Choi--Yuan block.  The construction in
\(\texttt{def:staircase-influence-map}\) specifies these as the exact
Proposition A.4 coefficients.  There is no cohort aggregation left, so
\(c_{0q}\) is precisely that single-block coefficient.

Because \(\mathcal K_n=\{0\}\), the definition of \(\Omega_n\) has only one
entry and gives
\[
\Omega_{00}
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  c_{0q}c_{0q}\sigma_{uv}^{2}
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  c_{0q}^{2}\sigma_{uv}^{2}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\),
\(\sigma_{uv}^{2}=\sigma_u^{2}\).  Consequently
\[
\Omega_{00}
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{0q}^{2}\sigma_u^{2},
\]
which is the heteroskedastic scalar influence variance of the one block.
Likewise, direct specialization of
\(\texttt{def:heteroskedastic-plugin}\) gives
\[
\widehat\Omega_{00}
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  \widehat c_{0q}^{\,2}\widehat\sigma_u^{2}.
\]
This is the corresponding unit-residual plug-in scalar variance: the unit
variance \(\widehat\sigma_u^2\) is the leave-one-cell-out residual-square
average specified in that definition.

It remains to identify the critical value.  The assumed positivity
\(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\) implies
\[
\widehat s_0=\sqrt{\widehat\Omega_{00}}>0,
\]
so studentization is well defined.  Conditional on \(Y\), the quantities
\(\widehat c_{0q}\), \(\widehat\sigma_u\), and \(\widehat s_0\) are fixed,
whereas the multipliers are independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and are
independent of \(Y\) by \(\texttt{def:multiplier-band}\).  Hence
\[
Z_0^\xi
:=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  \frac{\widehat c_{0q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_0}\xi_q
\ \bigg|\ Y
\sim N\!\left(
0,
\frac{\sum_q\widehat c_{0q}^{\,2}\widehat\sigma_u^2}
     {\widehat s_0^2}
\right)
=N(0,1),
\]
where the penultimate variance equals one because the numerator is
\(\widehat\Omega_{00}\) and
\(\widehat s_0^2=\widehat\Omega_{00}\).  Therefore
\[
W_n^\xi=|Z_0^\xi|,
\qquad
c_{1-\alpha,n}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2),
\]
with \(\Phi\) the standard-normal distribution function; the quantile is
finite and unique because \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  Finally,
\(\texttt{def:multiplier-band}\) reduces to
\[
\mathcal C_{n,0}
=\left[
\widehat\tau_0
\pm \Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\widehat s_0
\right],
\]
the ordinary two-sided studentized scalar interval.  Every equality above is
a finite-sample specialization of the declared definitions; no
growing-dimensional approximation or limit argument is used.

statements.statement:
Working over the baseline event-transfer slices
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), use the second-order staircase alignment
handle to derive a primitive block-ratio expression
\(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants
\(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that
\[
 c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
 \le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 \le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
\]
for every vanishing \(\eta_n\).  The upper-band implication is expressly
conditional on the unresolved feasible-score premise: there must exist
\(h_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
Under that premise, prove that
\(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) implies
\(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\).

Conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with
\(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^\dagger\) and
\(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which
\(\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero,
construct one complete selected pair in the common subclass
\(\mathfrak M^\cap\).  Its law coordinates must satisfy
\[
 \delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n),
 \qquad \liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0,
\]
and the witness itself must establish feasible-score stability for some
\(h_n\downarrow0\):
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
The derivation must first compute whether the balanced strong-factor
rank-one second-order remainder is
\(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so,
\(\Delta^\dagger\) must use the smaller attained scale.  Because the
published class permits \(M^R\ne0\), no upper-band conclusion is requested
for its full projection without an additional approximation-bias remainder.

obligation.what_is_open: Compute the exact signed second-order remainder of the specified Choi--Yuan estimator on a balanced rank-one complete array in \(\mathfrak M^\cap\), determine whether it is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\), and prove both an attained \(1-\eta_n\) quantile lower bound and feasible-score stability for the same counterarray.
obligation.obstruction: Proposition A.4 supplies an upper perturbation envelope after several norm inequalities, not an attained expansion.  The frozen estimator construction names the nuclear-norm and debiasing procedure but does not specify its tuning rule, KKT solution, or signed second-order map.  First-order coefficients and the two-horizon covariance witness therefore do not determine the nonlinear remainder or its sign.  The frozen assumptions also contain no rowwise loading rate for the leave-one-cell-out feasible score.
obligation.attempted: The class-scope obstruction was removed: the published model was encoded as an array plus one selected functional, the actual event-block correspondence was stated, and a balanced rank-one array was shown by direct rate substitution to lie in a nonempty common subclass.  On that array the primitive ratios, leverage, marginal scale, and published six hypotheses were computed.  These calculations still leave the estimator's second-order KKT remainder unidentified, so neither a reverse perturbation inequality nor undercoverage can be inferred from the first-order witness.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact nonprimitive frontier remains identified by the definitions:
\[
 \Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 =\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 \inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
For any \(u_n\) satisfying
\(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\le\eta_n\), the generic transfer theorem
gives a computable coverage bound after adding the displayed uniform
feasible-score premise.  In the i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel,
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\) further gives
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
 \mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)),
\]
and hence the one-sided quantile bound
\(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) whenever the
unsimplified source union bound is at most \(\eta_n\).  This does not give
a uniform upper bound over the whole baseline event-transfer slice.
The explicit balanced rank-one construction in
\(\texttt{prop:published-class-comparison}\) proves that the corrected
common subclass is nonempty and verifies both distinct families of rate
conditions.  It does not determine the nonlinear remainder: the frozen
construction of \(\widehat M^0\) omits the tuning rule, KKT solution, and
signed second-order debiasing expansion needed to compute its attained
quantile.  No reverse inequality, sign-aligned counterarray, or feasible
score rate for that counterarray has therefore been proved.

statements.justification: The remaining mathematical question is panel-specific attainability of the signed second-order remainder, not generic Gaussian approximation.

statements.statement: For one Choi--Yuan missing block with dimensions \(N_o\) and \(T_o\), missing-group size \(\vartheta_o\), i.i.d. centered homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, incoherence, signal, spectral-size, and missing-block conditions as stated in their Appendix A, Proposition A.4 gives, with probability at least \(1-O(\min\{N_o^{-9},T_o^{-9}\})\), a simultaneous entrywise linear expansion of every target imputation error into its donor-column and observed-row terms, with the maximum entry remainder bounded by a common constant times the three-term expression used here as \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) after setting \((N_o,T_o,\vartheta_o)=(N_{gk},T_g,n_g)\).

Let \(V\) and \(Y\) be centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), assume the coordinate variances of \(Y\) are bounded above and away from zero, and put \(\Delta_0=\max_{j,\ell}|\operatorname{Cov}(V_j,V_\ell)-\operatorname{Cov}(Y_j,Y_\ell)|\).  Lemma 3.1 gives
\[
 \sup_z\left|P\{\max_jV_j\le z\}-P\{\max_jY_j\le z\}\right|
 \le C\Delta_0^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\Delta_0)\}^{2/3},
\]
without a positive-minimum-eigenvalue requirement.

For a separable centered Gaussian process with unit pointwise variances and almost surely finite supremum, Theorem 2.1 bounds the Levy concentration function of the supremum at radius \(\varepsilon\) by \(4\varepsilon\) times one plus its expected supremum.  Corollary 2.1 gives the same bound for the supremum of the absolute value.  For a finite \(p\)-coordinate Gaussian vector this implies
\[
 \sup_zP\left\{\left|\max_{j\le p}|Z_j|-z\right|\le\varepsilon\right\}
 \le C\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(2p)}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement:
The following is the first main result of this paper.

Theorem 2.1 (Anti-concentration for suprema of separable Gaussian processes). Let X=(X_t)_{t∈T} be a separable Gaussian process indexed by a semimetric space T such that E[X_t]=0 and E[X_t²]=1 for all t∈T. Assume that sup_{t∈T} X_t<∞ a.s. Then a(X):=E[sup_{t∈T} X_t]∈[0,∞) and

    p_ε(X) ≤ 4 ε (a(X)+1),

for all ε≥0.

The similar conclusion holds for the concentration function of sup_{t∈T}|X_t|.

Corollary 2.1. Let X=(X_t)_{t∈T} be a separable Gaussian process indexed by a semimetric space T such that E[X_t]=0 and E[X_t²]=1 for all t∈T. Assume that sup_{t∈T}X_t<∞ a.s. Then a(|X|):=E[sup_{t∈T}|X_t|]∈[√(2/π),∞) and

    p_ε(|X|) ≤ 4 ε (a(|X|)+1),

for all ε≥0.

statements.statement:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) be independent centered random vectors in
\(\mathbb R^p\), where \(m\ge3\) and \(p\ge2\), and let
\(G\) be centered Gaussian with covariance
\(m^{-1}\sum_{q=1}^mE[x_qx_q^\top]\).  Suppose that \(B_m\ge1\),
\(E\exp(|x_{qj}|/B_m)\le2\) for all \(q,j\), and constants
\(0<b_1\le b_2<\infty\) satisfy
\[
 b_1^2\le \frac1m\sum_qE[x_{qj}^2],
 \qquad
 \frac1m\sum_qE[x_{qj}^4]\le B_m^2b_2^2
 \quad(j\le p).
\]
Then Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike (2022), Theorem 2.1, gives
\[
 \sup_{A\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}}
 \left|P\!\left\{m^{-1/2}\sum_qx_q\in A\right\}-P\{G\in A\}\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{B_m^2\log^5(pm)}m\right\}^{1/4},
\]
where \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}\) is the class of axis-aligned
hyperrectangles and \(C\) depends only on \(b_1,b_2\).  The theorem
places no positive-minimum-eigenvalue condition on the covariance matrix.

source.locator: Theorem 2.1, Annals of Statistics 50 (2022), doi:10.1214/22-AOS2193; arXiv:1912.10529v2, Section 2.3
source.verbatim_statement:
Second, let $b_1$ and $b_2$ be some strictly positive constants such that $b_1\leq b_2$ and let $\{B_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of constants such that $B_n \geq 1$ for all $n\geq 1$.

Condition E: For all $i=1,\dots,n$ and $j = 1,\dots,p$, we have
\[
\Ep[\exp(|X_{i j}|/B_n)]\leq 2.
\]

Condition M: For all $j=1,\dots,p$, we have
$$
b_1^2\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \Ep[X_{i j}^2]\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \Ep[X_{i j}^4]\leq B_n^2 b_2^2.
$$

Suppose that Conditions E and M are satisfied. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq: gaussian bound main}
\left|\Pr\left(T_n > c^G_{1-\alpha}\right) - \alpha\right| \leq C\left(\frac{B_n^2\log^5(p n)}{n}\right)^{1/4},
\end{equation}
where $C$ is a constant depending only on $b_1$ and $b_2$.

Since $a\in\mathbb R^p$ in the definition of $T_n$ is arbitrary, the bound can be equivalently stated as
$$
\sup_{A\in\mathcal A}\left|\Pr\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i \in A\right) - \Pr(G\in A)\right|\leq C\left(\frac{B_n^2\log^5(p n)}{n}\right)^{1/4},
$$
where $G\sim N(0_p,\Sigma_n)$ and $\mathcal A$ is the class of all hyper-rectangles in $\mathbb R^p$.

statements.statement:
In Choi--Yuan's published model the panel mean is
\(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+M^R\), where \(M^\star\) has rank \(r\), global
incoherence and condition-number indices are attached to \(M^\star\),
and \(\max_{i,t}|m^R_{it}|\to0\); the errors are i.i.d., centered,
homoskedastic, and sub-Gaussian.  Their staggered-adoption Theorem 3.2
fixes one scalar group average, indexed by one chosen
\((\mathcal G,t_0,\{\mathcal G_\ell\}_{\ell=0}^L)\), and imposes its six
conditions only for the adoption dates and blocks used by that chosen
functional.  Those conditions are three signal, spectral-size, and
group-size ratios, a local rate for \(M^R\), two normalized Gram bounds,
and two nonvanishing loading conditions.  The theorem does not impose
these six conditions simultaneously for every possible scalar functional
or every event horizon.

source.locator: Published model setup and Theorem 3.2, Journal of the American Statistical Association, doi:10.1080/01621459.2024.2380105; author manuscript in PubMed Central, PMC12413014
source.verbatim_statement:
Consider a panel data setting where M = (m_(it))_(1 ≤ i ≤ N, 1 ≤ t ≤ T)
is a N × T approximately low rank matrix. We assume that
M = M^(⋆) + M^(R) where M^(⋆) = (m_(it)^(⋆))_(1 ≤ i ≤ N, 1 ≤ t ≤ T) is a
matrix of rank r(≪min{N,T}) and
M^(R) = (m_(it)^(R))_(1 ≤ i ≤ N, 1 ≤ t ≤ T) is a low rank approximation
error such that max_(it)|m_(it)^(R)|→0. We use i as the cross-section
index and t as the time index. Following the convention of the matrix
completion literature, we shall assume that the singular vectors of the
low rank matrix M^(⋆) are incoherent in that there is a μ ≥ 1 such that
${\parallel U_{M^{\star}} \parallel}_{2,\infty} \leq \sqrt{\mu r/N},{\parallel V_{M^{\star}} \parallel}_{2,\infty} \leq \sqrt{\mu r/T}$
where U_(M^(⋆)) and V_(M^(⋆)) denote the left and right singular vectors
of M^(⋆), respectively. The incoherence condition requires the singular
vectors to be de-localized, in the sense that entries are not dominated
by a small number of rows or columns. Instead of M, we observe a subset
of the entries of Y = M + E where E = (ϵ_(it))_(1 ≤ i ≤ N, 1 ≤ t ≤ T) is
a noise matrix following the assumption below.

Assumption [Noise].

ϵ_(it) are independent, identically distributed zero-mean, sub-Gaussian
random variables, i.e.,
𝔼[ϵ_(it)²] = σ², 𝔼[exp(sϵ_(it))] ≤ exp(Cs²σ²), ∀s ∈ ℝ and some constant
C > 0.

The independence assumption is a common assumption in the matrix
completion literature. In the model, the dependence in y_(it) can be
explained by the low rank part m_(it) in which we can allow arbitrary
correlations. As noted in our empirical application, this low rank term
works as an interactive fixed effect term, and together with additional
control variables, it may account for the large part of the dependence
structure in y_(it). In addition, the simulation experiment in Section
A.4 of the supplement shows that if the dependence in noise terms is
mild, our estimator and the corresponding inference method work quite
well. However, because our proof strategy is based on the leave-one-out
technique (see, e.g., Chen et al. (2019b, 2020a,b)), allowing dependency
in noise is challenging. Since this is beyond the scope of this paper,
we leave this to future research. Additionally, to relax the identical
distribution assumption, we present the extension of our theory to the
case of heteroskedasticity in Section G.2 of the supplement.
Staggered Adaption.

More generally, consider the case of staggered adoption when there are D
number of adoption time points, T₁ < T₂ < ⋯ < T_(D), and D number of
corresponding groups of treated units, G₁, …, G_(D). As in the previous
situation, suppose that we are interested in inference for the group
average at time t₀. Denote by N₀ the number of units that are untreated
until t₀, and by T₀ the number of time periods where {1,…,N₀} is
untreated, respectively.

We proceed by first splitting 𝒢 into smaller groups, denoted by
{𝒢_(l)}_(0 ≤ l ≤ L) with the convention that 𝒢₀ = 𝒢 ∩ {1,⋯,N₀}. In doing
so, we want to make sure that all units in each subgroup
{𝒢_(l)}_(1 ≤ l ≤ L) have the same adoption time point, e.g.,
𝒢_(l) ⊆ G_(d_(l)), as illustrated in Figure 5. Denote by
D_(𝒢) = {d_(l):1≤l≤L} and by ψ_(min,O_(d)) the smallest singular value
of the submatrix
M_(O_(d))^(⋆) = (m_(it)^(⋆))_(1 ≤ i ≤ N₀, 1 ≤ t ≤ T_(d)).

Theorem 3.2. Assume that for any d ∈ D_(𝒢) ∪ {0} and l = 1, …, L,

i.  $\sigma\kappa^{\frac{23}{4}}\mu^{\frac{3}{2}}r^{\frac{3}{2}}\sqrt{N_{0}}max\left\{ {N_{0}\sqrt{\text{log}\mspace{9mu} N_{0}},T_{d}\sqrt{\text{log}\mspace{9mu} T_{d}}} \right\} = o_{p}\left( {\psi_{\text{min},O_{d}}\text{min}\left\{ {N_{0},T_{d}} \right\}} \right);$

ii. $\kappa^{\frac{11}{2}}\mu^{3}r^{3}\sqrt{N_{0}}max\left\{ {\sqrt{N_{0}\text{log}^{3}N_{0}},\sqrt{T_{d}\text{log}^{3}T_{d}}} \right\} = o_{p}\left( {\text{min}\left\{ {N_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}},T_{d}^{\frac{3}{2}}} \right\}} \right);$

iii. $\left| \mathcal{G}_{l} \right|\kappa^{\frac{17}{4}}\mu^{\frac{5}{2}}r^{\frac{5}{2}}max\left\{ {\sqrt{N_{0}\text{log}\mspace{9mu} N_{0}},\sqrt{T_{d_{l}}\text{log}\mspace{9mu} T_{d_{l}}}} \right\} = o_{p}\left( {\sqrt{N_{0}}\text{min}\left\{ {N_{0},T_{d_{l}}} \right\}} \right);$

iv. $\text{max}_{i \in \mathcal{U}_{l},t \in \mathcal{T}_{l}}\left| m_{it}^{R} \right| = o_{p}\left( \frac{\sigma}{\kappa^{\frac{5}{2}}\mu r\text{max}\left\{ {\sqrt{N_{0}},\sqrt{T_{d_{l}}}} \right\}} \right);$

v.  there are constants C₁, c₂ > 0 such that
    $$c_{1} \leq \lambda_{\text{min}}\left( {\frac{N}{N_{0}}\sum\limits_{i \leq N_{0}}u_{i}u_{i}^{\top}} \right) \leq \lambda_{max}\left( {\frac{N}{N_{0}}\sum\limits_{i \leq N_{0}}u_{i}u_{i}^{\top}} \right) \leq c_{2},$$
    $$c_{1} \leq \lambda_{\text{min}}\left( {\frac{T}{T_{d}}\sum\limits_{t \leq T_{d}}v_{t}v_{t}^{\top}} \right) \leq \lambda_{max}\left( {\frac{T}{T_{d}}\sum\limits_{t \leq T_{d}}v_{t}v_{t}^{\top}} \right) \leq c_{2};$$

vi. $\sqrt{N}{\parallel {\overset{‾}{u}}_{\mathcal{G}} \parallel} \geq c$
    and $\sqrt{T}{\parallel v_{t_{0}} \parallel} \geq c$ for some
    constant c > 0.

    Then, we have
    $$\mathcal{V}_{\mathcal{G}}^{- \frac{1}{2}}\left( {\frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}|}{\sum\limits_{i \in \mathcal{G}}{\overset{\hat{}}{m}}_{it_{0}}} - \frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}|}{\sum\limits_{i \in \mathcal{G}}m_{it_{0}}}} \right)\overset{D}{\rightarrow}\mathcal{N}(0,1),$$

    where
    $$V_{\mathcal{G}} = \sigma^{2}\left( {{\overline{u}}_{\mathcal{G}}^{\top}\left( {\sum\limits_{j \leq N_{0}}{u_{j}u_{j}^{\top}}} \right)^{- 1}{\overline{u}}_{\mathcal{G}} + \frac{1}{|\mathcal{G}|}v_{t_{0}}^{\top}\left\lbrack {{\sum\limits_{d \in D_{\mathcal{G}} \cup {\{ 0\}}}\frac{\left| {G_{d} \cap \mathcal{G}} \right|}{|\mathcal{G}|}}\left( {\sum\limits_{s \leq T_{d}}{v_{s}v_{s}^{\top}}} \right)^{- 1}} \right\rbrack v_{t_{0}}} \right),$$

    with the convention that G₀ = {1,…,N₀}.

statements.statement:
After projecting the published array-plus-selected-functional objects to
their law arrays on the common staggered-panel sample space, neither the
baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) nor its band
subclass \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) contains the published Choi--Yuan
class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}_{\mathrm{sel}}\), and the published
class contains neither event-transfer class.  The common subclass
\(\mathfrak M^\cap\) is nonempty.  Its event-block/published-block
correspondence is
\(N_0=|J_{gk}|\), \(T_d=|S_g|\),
\(N_{gk}=|I_g\cup J_{gk}|\), and \(T_g=|S_g|+1\); membership requires
both, not an identification of, the two families of rate inequalities.
A converse proved on \(\mathfrak M^\cap\) transfers upward to the
published approximate-rank class.  In contrast, the event-transfer
upper-band theorem does not transfer to the full published class without
adding the approximation bias generated by \(M^R\) to the remainder
event.
statements.proof_tex:
The comparison is well typed after applying the law projection in
\(\texttt{def:choi-yuan-published-selected-class}\): both sides are then
sets of complete laws on the same \(N\)-by-\(T\) staggered-panel sample
space.  The source scope encoded by
\(\texttt{lem:choi-yuan-published-selected-scope}\) verifies that the
published object carries only one selected scalar functional and permits
\(M^R\ne0\), while the definitions of the two event-transfer classes
require exact low rank, blockwise uniform geometry, rowwise variance
structure, variance replication, and a maximum-cell leverage envelope.

For the first strict noncontainment, start from a balanced rank-one
published signal \(M^\star=\mathbf1_d\mathbf1_d^\top\) with i.i.d.
\(N(0,1)\) errors and the selected functional used below.  Let
\(M^R=q_dI_d\), where \(q_d>0\) decreases sufficiently fast to satisfy
both the global approximation requirement and the selected local
condition (iv).  All six conditions concerning \(M^\star\) are unchanged,
but \(M^{\mathrm{pub}}=M^\star+q_dI_d\) has rank \(d\).  Since the
event-transfer classes require rank \(r<\min\{N,T\}=d\), this published
law is in neither event-transfer class.  This witness uses no fixed bound
on the published \(\kappa\), \(\mu\), or noise variance.

For the reverse strict noncontainment, use the exact balanced rank-one
array below but replace the i.i.d. errors by independent Gaussian errors
whose unit variances alternate between \(1\) and \(2\) and are constant
over time.  The fixed variance bounds, row heteroskedasticity, replication,
and all event-transfer rate conditions continue to hold.  No selected
functional can turn unequal Gaussian variances into i.i.d. homoskedastic
noise.  Hence this array belongs to the band event-transfer class, and
therefore also to its baseline class, but its law is outside the published
projection.  The two noncontainments prove incomparability.

It remains to prove that \(\mathfrak M^\cap\ne\varnothing\).  Let
\(d=d_n\to\infty\) be even, put \(N=T=d\),
\(b=\lfloor d^{1/3}\rfloor\), \(g=\lfloor d/2\rfloor\), and
\(K=\lfloor d^{1/10}\rfloor\).  Let one cohort of size \(b\) adopt at
\(g\), let the other \(d-b\) units never adopt, set \(x_i=z_t=1\),
\(M^R=0\), and take i.i.d. \(N(0,1)\) errors.  Select
\(\phi_n=(I_g,g,\{I_g\})\).  Every event block has
\[
 N_{gk}=d,\qquad T_g=g,\qquad
 \psi_{gk}=\sqrt{dg},\qquad \kappa_{gk}=\mu_{gk}=r=1,
 \qquad A_{gk}=d-b,\quad B_g=g-1.
\]
Thus both Gram bounds hold with constants bounded away from zero and
infinity.  Direct substitution gives the event-transfer ratios
\[
 O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log d}{d}}\right),\qquad
 O\!\left(\frac{\log^3d}{d}\right),\qquad
 O(d^{-2/3})
\]
for the signal, spectral-size, and missing-block conditions, respectively,
and the variance-replication ratio is
\(O(d^{-1/2}\log^{5/2}d)\).

For every horizon, the \(b\) treated target coefficients are \(1/b\),
the \(d-b\) donor target coefficients are \(-1/(d-b)\), and the
\(b(g-1)\) treated pre-period coefficients are
\(-1/[b(g-1)]\).  Therefore
\[
 s_k^2=\frac1b+\frac1{d-b}+\frac1{b(g-1)}\asymp b^{-1},
 \qquad L_n(K)\asymp b^{-1/2}=d^{-1/6}.
\]
Moreover \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\le Kd+b(g-1)\le Cd^{4/3}\),
so
\[
 L_n(K)^2\log^5((2K\vee3)m)=O(d^{-1/3}\log^5d)\to0.
\]
The three terms in \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) have orders
\[
 O\!\left(\frac{\log d}{d}\right),\qquad
 O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log d}}d\right),\qquad
 O\!\left(\frac{b\sqrt{\log d}}{d^{3/2}}\right).
\]
Since \(s_k^{-1}\asymp\sqrt b\), it follows that
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}
 =O(d^{-5/6}\log^{3/2}d)\to0.
\]
Because every fixed envelope in the class is positive, \(d_n\) can be
chosen recursively large enough that all five baseline ratios, and even
the band remainder ratio, are below their prescribed envelopes at index
\(n\).

For the selected published functional, \(N_0=d-b\asymp d\),
\(T_d=g-1\asymp d\), and
\(\psi^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\min,O_d}=\sqrt{N_0T_d}\asymp d\).  Substitution into its first
three conditions gives, respectively,
\[
 O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log d}{d}}\right),\qquad
 O\!\left(\frac{\log^{3/2}d}{\sqrt d}\right),\qquad
 O\!\left(d^{-2/3}\sqrt{\log d}\right),
\]
which vanish.  Condition (iv) is zero.  The normalized row and column
Gram matrices in condition (v) equal \(1\), because the global singular
vectors have entries \(d^{-1/2}\), and condition (vi) also equals one:
\(\sqrt d\,|\bar u^{\mathrm{pub}}_{I_g}|=\sqrt d\,|v_g^{\mathrm{pub}}|=1\).  Thus the array satisfies
all six selected-functional conditions and every uniform event-block
condition.  It belongs to \(\mathfrak M^\cap\), proving nonemptiness and
the stated actual block correspondence.

Finally, set inclusion gives the transfer direction.  Any lower-bound or
counterexample law in \(\mathfrak M^\cap\) is also a law admitted by the
published class.  An upper theorem on the exact-rank event-transfer class
does not cover a nonzero \(M^R\); its deterministic bias appears in the
target-centered statistic and must be included in \(\rho_n\) or in a
separate approximation-bias event.  No such term is present in the frozen
band, so upper validity cannot be transferred to the full published class.
statements.justification: This proposition prevents the event-transfer assumptions from being misattributed to Choi--Yuan and supplies a legal common subclass for any eventual converse.
statements.gap: The published model and the event-transfer model differ in rank approximation, noise structure, geometry, functional quantification, and growing-path envelopes.
statements.consumer: A counterarray in the common subclass transfers upward to the published model, while upper validity requires a separate approximation-bias argument.
